title: 6 Goblins + 4 Draenei

sources.label: HOW TO PLAY New Patch 6 Goblins + 4 Darenei In Auto Chess

body:
# 6 Goblins + 4 Draenei

This is a three-star hyper-roll comp that wins through pure damage and sustain. The engine is the Draenei trait: at four Draenei, whenever a friendly piece takes more than 100 cumulative healing, that healing is converted into AoE pure damage splashed onto nearby enemies. Because Goblins and Draenei are all cheap one- and two-cost units, you can roll them to three-star at low levels, then bolt on heavy healing (especially Mekansm) so every heal doubles as a burst. The patch dropping Shadow Demon to a one-cost is what makes the four-Draenei package roll-friendly on a losing streak.

Timbersaw is the durable centerpiece — he carries every top item and face-tanks while the pure damage does the killing. The comp is fully online once everything is three-star and you reach level 9-10.

## Core Units

| Unit | Cost | Synergies | Role |
|------|------|-----------|------|
| Timbersaw | 2 | Goblin, Mech | Carry / tank, holds all key items |
| Clockwerk | 1 | Goblin, Mech | Cheap Goblin + Mech body |
| Tinker | 1 | Goblin, Mech | Cheap Goblin + Mech body |
| Techies | 5 | Goblin, Mech | Sixth Goblin, big AoE, wants Refresher |
| Alchemist | 4 | Goblin, Ogre, Warlock | Goblin + a Warlock for lifesteal |
| Snapfire | 4 | Goblin, Knight | Rounds out the six Goblins |
| Shadow Demon | 1 | Demon, Draenei, Priest | One-cost Draenei core |
| Bounty Hunter | 1 | Draenei, Goblin, Hunter | Doubles as Goblin and Draenei; first-blood gold |
| Dark Seer | 2 | Draenei, Warlock | Draenei + Warlock |
| Dawnbreaker | 3 | Draenei, Knight | Fourth Draenei — don't over-invest, she caps at two-star value |

With Clockwerk, Tinker, Timbersaw and Techies you also pick up the Mech shields as a free bonus, and Alchemist + Dark Seer start the Warlock lifesteal you extend late.

## Items

- **Mekansm (tier 3)** is the single best item here — the 500 heal it throws is exactly what the Draenei trait converts into pure AoE damage. Stack it with **Refresher Orb (tier 4)** on a caster and you double every burst.
- **Timbersaw** is your item sink: Mekansm, Giants Ring (tier 4) for the block/regen-as-offense, and Radiance (tier 4) for constant pure damage that pairs with Warlock lifesteal.
- **Giants Ring (tier 4)** and **Radiance (tier 4)** are the tier-four items to roll toward once you can craft; both convert survivability into damage.
- Early game, prioritise armor and regeneration (Vanguard, tier 2) so you can survive to the three-star spike.

## Leveling / Roll Plan

- **Early (rounds 1-10):** The cheap one-cost Shadow Demon makes a losing streak trivial to hold — take it, bank gold, and collect your Goblins/Draenei. Sell a spare unit if it locks in a clean interest breakpoint.
- **Dismissals (after round 10):** Dismiss Warriors for the best rate on your low-cost cores (about 22-26 gold); Trolls are the cheaper fallback dismissal.
- **Rolling (round 15+):** Don't roll before round 15 — rates are worse. Then roll at a low level for three-stars. Manage bench space carefully: don't over-flood the board while rolling, or the auto-sell timer can eat your two-star units.
- **Leveling out:** Once your cores are three-star, push level 6 → 7 → 8 → 9. Level 9 is the biggest spike; get there around round 30 and add the wizard/Warlock layer.

## Positioning / Matchup Notes

Keep Timbersaw and the healing cores central so the Draenei pure-damage splash lands on the most enemies. Late, extend into Warlock (Alchemist + Dark Seer + Warlock, plus a relic-granted synergy) for lifesteal, or Naga (via Naga Siren) when you face mages and need magic resistance.

The comp face-tanks physical damage and out-sustains warriors and assassins. Its real counters are other sources of **pure damage** — Sven, Demons, or Havoc — that ignore your armor, plus Doom shutting off Timbersaw's healing. Against those, add magic resistance and lean on your own pure-damage output rather than trading heals.
